Cost-per-swipe and break-even tables (e.g. Unlimited $32.40/$22.68/$16.20; Traditional $29.79/$20.85/$14.90; Choice $24.52/$17.17; Basic $18.94; break-even 341/220, 313/202, 258/167, 199/129)

fact_check.claim: A lunch at the door costs $15.50 (Feb 2025 Sun column)
fact_check.note: The column does say $15.50 for non-plan diners, lunch Monday to Saturday. But it is a hard price resting only on a student newspaper and it is the break-even benchmark of the whole article. It needs an official Cornell Dining source, or the article should link the official guest/door price.

fact_check.claim: Maia Mehring, a sophomore: Okenshields is the only Central Campus option accepting swipes; students often run out of BRBs mid-semester
fact_check.note: Author is Class of 2027 (ILR); both claims are in the column and are attributed as her claims.

fact_check.claim: Nile Jones, then a junior, said she ate fewer than 10 meals a week and unused swipes cost $1,000 to $2,000 a year
fact_check.note: The column says 'I struggle to eat more than 10 meals a week', i.e. about 10 or fewer, not 'fewer than 10'. The $1,000 to $2,000 figure and junior status are correct.

fact_check.claim: Andrea Miramontes Serrano, then a freshman: Saturday grocery trip cost $147, about $400 spent on food; she also said the plan's convenience can be 'too expensive'
fact_check.note: $147, about $400 and freshman status are right, but the 'too expensive' line was said by another student, S. Aiyer '24, not the author. Misattributed quote.

fact_check.claim: 2011 College Confidential thread: several posters advised off-campus students against meal plans; one called plans a 'ripoff'
fact_check.note: Thread is July-August 2011; posters hermanns ('major ripoff') and Caillebotte advise against plans.

beats_top.why: The #1 result is a 2019 opinion column with outdated prices and no plan-by-plan math, so a student gets current 2026-27 rates, a cost-per-swipe table and a by-situation section from us. The page should be right on every number and clear which choices a student actually has before it fully wins.
changes: Fix the $672 vs $548 error and the misattributed and overstated student claims so the numbers a student relies on are right.
Back the $15.50 door price with an official Cornell Dining source, since the whole break-even verdict rests on it.

Say plainly that Bear Choice and Bear Basic are open to on-campus students only if enrolled before Summer 2021, and that the fall 2026 reduction deadline has passed so the next one is February 3, 2027.

fixes: In the 'Transfer student or on-campus junior' bullet, change the difference between Unlimited and Bear Traditional from $672 to $548 per year ($7,604 vs $7,056); source https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/dining/meal-plans-rates/undergraduate-meal-plans

In the Nile Jones sentence, change 'said she ate fewer than 10 meals a week' to 'wrote that she struggles to eat more than 10 meals a week'; source https://www.cornellsun.com/article/2019/04/jones-stop-forcing-west-campus-residents-to-buy-unlimited-meal-swipes

In the Andrea Miramontes Serrano sentence, remove 'She also said the plan's convenience can be "too expensive."' or attribute it correctly to another student, S. Aiyer '24, who is quoted in the column; source https://cornellsun.com/2020/10/26/a-skidmore-medal-topped-with-runny-pasta-freshman-year-with-zero-meal-plan

Find the current door/guest lunch price on an official Cornell Dining page (for example the dining.cornell.edu or scl.cornell.edu guest meal or dining room rates page), cite it inline for the $15.50 figure in the first paragraph and the break-even section, and keep the 2025 Sun column only as secondary attribution. If no official price can be found, say in the first paragraph and the caveat that the $15.50 is a student-reported figure, and show the break-even table at the $10 and an additional official or clearly labeled alternative value.

In the 'Off campus' bullet and the Bear Basic sentence in the break-even section, add that Bear Choice and Bear Basic are available to on-campus undergraduates only if they enrolled at Cornell before Summer 2021 (so on-campus transfers and juniors cannot buy them); source https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/dining/meal-plans-rates/undergraduate-meal-plans

In the 'Transfer student or on-campus junior' bullet, state that the September 9, 2026 fall deadline has already passed (today is November 7, 2026) and that the next reduction deadline is February 3, 2027; source https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/dining/meal-plans-rates/deadlines-terms
